title: SRE Incident Response Agent
subtitle: Investigate incidents with cited telemetry, explicit source gaps and human-approved mitigation.
theme: Agents and Copilots in Real Workflows
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Read-only boundary and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Open with query-anything, change-nothing; list the eight numbers and the oracle.

practice_prompts.label: From 400 alerts to a cited summary
practice_prompts.hint: Trace dedupe, context, parallel typed reads and the 30-second budget.

practice_prompts.label: Proposal, approval and gateway
practice_prompts.hint: Name every proposal field, who approves, what blocks it and the gateway order.

practice_prompts.label: Degraded telemetry, evaluation and rollout
practice_prompts.hint: Say what the summary shows when metrics are down, the falsifying metric and the rollout stages.

rubric: Opens with the read-only boundary and explains why a ten-second approval beats an autonomous rollback.
Names dependency inversion and keeps EMPTY and UNAVAILABLE distinct, with source coverage in the summary.
Collapses the 400-alert burst with rules or a small model and per-service caps before any strong-model call.
Lists the proposal fields, computes blast radius from topology, and blocks on missing blast radius, simulation or approval.
Gives the gateway order with authorisation before validation and never explains a denial to the model.
States the 30-second budget in slices and says provider and telemetry quotas bind at 10x, not the model.
Gates on hypothesis precision from post-incident review and rolls out shadow, then live read-only, then approved low-risk actions.

editorial_review.evidence: Compared all 55 captured sections of the SRE case against the earlier draft section by section. The draft had silently dropped the weak/average/strong answer tiers, the five-person people map, the non-goals exception for draft timeline and approved Jira writes, the eight 'lines that carry the round', the full two-minute spoken answer, the recovery-moves figure's content, one of five weak-answer repairs, and the DENIED/INVALID confusion; all are restored. Added a numbered checkout-5xx trace to the brief, plain definitions (on-call, commander, blast radius, change freeze, dry run, MTTA, MoSCoW, fail closed), split failure handling into a walkthrough step plus a ladder dive, and recaptioned all ten source figures from their actual SVG labels (the gateway and typed-result figures are flagged as generic refund/order examples). Removed an unsupported 'model-serving CPU' claim; the 28-second upper-bound sum and the idempotency reconciliation caveat are labelled as additions. Old tab navigation is consolidated, not reproduced. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): two reused pattern figures show order/refund examples inside an incident-agent case → captions no longer attribute the mismatch to the source; they state neutrally that the figure's example is generic and how the same mechanism applies here (figures are hashed originals, left unchanged).
